why: Checks 1 and 2 are fine. Every assertion in them follows from the expect line's words: zero and space padding, exact width, and s unchanged when it is width long or longer. Two checks break the criterion. Check 4's expect line is only "npm test passes", which exit 0 satisfies. Its PASS condition also requires that it "reports `# fail 0`". That is an exact-output rule, and it can wrongly fail: node --test's spec reporter (the default in newer Node) prints "ℹ fail 0", not "# fail 0". Check 3's script only counts a heading that starts with the function name (`^#{1,6}\s+`?name\b`). That fixes a heading format the words "a section for every function" don't require: a section headed "## Using padLeft" would fail. Both extra rules belong under Advisory, not in PASS/FAIL.
